dynamicPorts.description: Declares conditional/expandable port groups whose visibility depends on parameter values (see declaredPortGroups). Some ports are discovered at runtime from user code, parameters or connected components, and are pushed to the editor per instance; the static port list below is incomplete for such instances.

declaredPortGroups.condition: idSource = explicit OR idSource NOT SET
declaredPortGroups.name: conditionalports/extended

idSource: From repeater: at the frame's end it binds to the record of the row it sits in
otherwise: kept; the record stays bound until the next Id
repeaterComponent: under From repeater: at the frame's end it binds to the record of that repeater's row (blank: the nearest)
otherwise: kept, and read only under From repeater
modelId: always: the record with that id is bound now (a record handed in, by its id; an empty id binds nothing), and Id is sent again
targetId: always: kept, unchecked, for the next Do — the record at the other end of the relation; it must have been loaded (from a Query Records or Record), or the Do fails with its class unknown
store: always: no check at the press — it joins the frame's batch, and at the end of the frame one call answers every press: Done for each (what the backend hands back is written onto the record), or Error and Failure for each (no Class, no Relation, no Target Record Id, no record bound, a target record never loaded, no backend, or the backend refuses)

inputs.name: runOnChange-value
inputs.description: Whether a new value on Value re-runs this node. On by default; untick to make this input passive so only the control signal runs it

inputs.name: saveValue
inputs.description: Stores the latest value now. This is additional to Value storing on change; untick Value under Run On Value Change to stop that

inputs.name: treatEmptyAs
inputs.description: Back-compat for graphs written before Variables were nullable. `null` (default) keeps a cleared value distinguishable from a real false. Choosing another option restores the pre-NDA-003 coercion for authors who relied on it.

inputs.name: treatUnchangedAs
inputs.description: What this node reports when the action was valid and there was nothing to do. Unchanged (the default) keeps it a third outcome of its own. Done suits a project whose chains should carry on either way. Completed fires whatever this is set to.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The empty-value contract (dev-docs/reference/EMPTY-VALUE-CONTRACT.md): `undefined` abstains and leaves the Variable's stored value untouched. `null` is a real value — it clears the Variable, is stored, and fires Changed. What "cleared" is stored as is controlled by `Treat empty as` (null by default).

outputs.name: changed
outputs.description: Fires whenever the stored value actually changed, however it was reached — including Value writing straight through under Run On Value Change. It is a value-level event, not the outcome of a Set

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires when a Set stored a value the Variable was not already holding

outputs.name: savedValue
outputs.description: Can be `null` — a cleared Variable (see `value`'s description) stores and emits null by default, not this type's zero value, unless `Treat empty as` says otherwise.

outputs.name: unchanged
outputs.description: Fires when a Set stored the value it already held, so nothing changed. ⚠️ With Value left ticked under Run On Value Change this is the common case, because Value has already stored by the time Set fires

value: undefined: ignored → Changed stays silent
the same as the last one, or Run On Value Change unticked: held for the next Set → Changed stays silent
a new value that converts to what is already stored: held, nothing changes → Changed stays silent
a new value, with Run On Value Change ticked: stored straight away (an empty one as Treat Empty As says) → Changed
saveValue: always: at the end of the frame the last Value is stored — Changed and Done if that changed it, otherwise Unchanged (or what Treat Unchanged As says)

inputs.name: falseString

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: Which of the two strings to publish: false, 0, empty text or no value picks String for false; anything else picks String for true

inputs.name: trueString
inputs.description: Text published on Current Value while Selector is true

outputs.name: currentValue
outputs.description: String for true or String for false, whichever Selector currently picks

outputs.name: inputChanged
outputs.description: Fires when Selector flips, after Current Value has been updated

trueString: the same text: nothing, not even a send
new text: kept, and sent on Current Value if Selector picks String for true
falseString: the same text: nothing, not even a send
new text: kept, and sent on Current Value if Selector picks String for false
input: the same value: nothing, not even a send → Selector Changed stays silent
a different value, even one that picks the same string: Current Value follows → Selector Changed

declaredPortGroups.condition: shape = circle OR shape NOT SET
shape = square OR shape = triangle OR shape = polygon OR shape = star

accept.rule: a data attribute name: "data-", then a lowercase letter or digit, then lowercase letters, digits, ".", "_" or "-"

variables.name: one of the names listed in the `dataAttributes` parameter; a data attribute name: "data-", then a lowercase letter or digit, then lowercase letters, digits, ".", "_" or "-"

parameterEncoding.notes: Every port is listed in `inputs`/`outputs` above except the ones named by a list parameter (the patterns here): `dynamicPorts.declaredPortGroups` says which parameter values reveal which listed port, and holds the `namedports/derived` rule that turns each listed name into a port.

mounted: a change: the element is put on the page, or taken off it, at the next paint
the value it already holds: nothing
scrollIntoView: always: the page, or the scrolling Group holding it, scrolls until the element can be seen
visible: always: shown or hidden at the next paint, its space kept; hidden, it takes no pointer
opacity: always: how see-through it is; at exactly 0 it takes no pointer, and an act goes to what is behind it
pointerEventsMode: Inherit: its own pointer style comes off
Explicit: the last Pointer Events Enabled is written back (on, before one was set)
pointerEventsEnabled: always, whatever the mode: off, the pointer passes through to what is behind it
draggable: always: on, every element it draws can be picked up, by pointer or keyboard; off, the one on the page cannot
dragValue: always: read by the zone it is dropped on, which reports it as Dropped Value
dragKind: always: read by a zone with an Accept Kind as it is dragged over one
holdToDrag: always: read at the next press — whether it must be held before it picks up
holdTime: always: read at the next held press — how many seconds it is held before it picks up
acceptDrops: on: a Draggable can be dropped here
off while a drag is over it: the drag leaves it — Is Drop Target goes false
off: nothing can be dropped here

declaredPortGroups.condition: flexDirection != none AND scrollEnabled = true AND nativeScroll = false
flexDirection != none AND scrollEnabled = true AND scrollSnapEnabled = true
flexDirection = row OR flexWrap = wrap OR flexWrap = wrap-reverse
flexDirection = column OR flexWrap = wrap OR flexWrap = wrap-reverse
sizeMode = explicit OR sizeMode = contentHeight OR sizeMode NOT SET
sizeMode = explicit OR sizeMode = contentWidth OR sizeMode NOT SET
borderStyle = solid OR borderStyle = dashed OR borderStyle = dotted
borderLeftStyle = solid OR borderLeftStyle = dashed OR borderLeftStyle = dotted OR borderStyle = solid OR borderStyle = dashed OR borderStyle = dotted
borderTopStyle = solid OR borderTopStyle = dashed OR borderTopStyle = dotted OR borderStyle = solid OR borderStyle = dashed OR borderStyle = dotted
borderRightStyle = solid OR borderRightStyle = dashed OR borderRightStyle = dotted OR borderStyle = solid OR borderStyle = dashed OR borderStyle = dotted
borderBottomStyle = solid OR borderBottomStyle = dashed OR borderBottomStyle = dotted OR borderStyle = solid OR borderStyle = dashed OR borderStyle = dotted

accept.rule: a data attribute name: "data-", then a lowercase letter or digit, then lowercase letters, digits, ".", "_" or "-"

variables.name: one of the names listed in the `dataAttributes` parameter; a data attribute name: "data-", then a lowercase letter or digit, then lowercase letters, digits, ".", "_" or "-"

parameterEncoding.notes: Every port is listed in `inputs`/`outputs` above except the ones named by a list parameter (the patterns here): `dynamicPorts.declaredPortGroups` says which parameter values reveal which listed port, and holds the `namedports/derived` rule that turns each listed name into a port.

mounted: a change: the element is put on the page, or taken off it, at the next paint
the value it already holds: nothing
scrollIntoView: always: the page, or the scrolling Group holding it, scrolls until the element can be seen
as: always: the HTML element the next paint draws (a div when empty) — a new Tag draws a new element
visible: always: shown or hidden at the next paint, its space kept; hidden, it takes no pointer
opacity: always: how see-through it is; at exactly 0 it takes no pointer, and an act goes to what is behind it
pointerEventsMode: Inherit: its own pointer style comes off
Explicit: the last Pointer Events Enabled is written back (on, before one was set)
pointerEventsEnabled: always, whatever the mode: off, the pointer passes through to what is behind it
blockTouch: always: on, a pointer act that lands here goes no further — the nodes it sits inside do not hear it
draggable: always: on, every element it draws can be picked up, by pointer or keyboard; off, the one on the page cannot
dragValue: always: read by the zone it is dropped on, which reports it as Dropped Value
dragKind: always: read by a zone with an Accept Kind as it is dragged over one
holdToDrag: always: read at the next press — whether it must be held before it picks up
holdTime: always: read at the next held press — how many seconds it is held before it picks up
acceptDrops: on: a Draggable can be dropped here
off while a drag is over it: the drag leaves it — Is Drop Target goes false
off: nothing can be dropped here
acceptKind: always: read as a drag comes over it — a source of another kind does not light it up
acceptFileDrops: on: a file dragged from the desktop can be dropped here
off: no file can be dropped here, and a drag over it is forgotten — Is Dragging Over goes false if it was true
acceptedFileTypes: always: read at a drop — which files count as accepted
focus: off the page: nothing is listed, and the editor is told → Unchanged; Focused stays silent
off the page, after outcomes this frame resolved and has not reported: nothing is listed, the editor is told, and Unchanged comes after them → Focused stays silent
already listed as focused → Done; Focused stays silent
already listed, after outcomes this frame has not reported: Done comes after them → Focused stays silent
on the page: listed as focused → Focused, Done
on the page, after outcomes this frame has not reported: listed as focused, and Done comes after them → Focused
scrollToIndex.index: always: read when Scroll To Index runs, at the end of the frame
scrollToElement.element: always: read when Scroll To Element runs, at the end of the frame
scrollToIndex.do: always: runs at the end of the frame — Done when there is a child at Index, else Failure; before the Group is on the page it waits for it (at most 16 wait, and the oldest pushed out reports Failure)
scrollToElement.do: always: runs at the end of the frame, waiting as Scroll To Index does — Done when Element is empty (nothing to scroll to), Failure for a value that is not an element

warnings.focus/not-mounted: the last Focus arrived while it was not on the page

parameterEncoding.notes: Every port is listed in `inputs`/`outputs` above except the ones named by a list parameter (the patterns here): `dynamicPorts.declaredPortGroups` says which parameter values reveal which listed port, and holds the `namedports/derived` rule that turns each listed name into a port.

mounted: a change: the element is put on the page, or taken off it, at the next paint
the value it already holds: nothing
scrollIntoView: always: the page, or the scrolling Group holding it, scrolls until the element can be seen
visible: always: shown or hidden at the next paint, its space kept; hidden, it takes no pointer
opacity: always: how see-through it is; at exactly 0 it takes no pointer, and an act goes to what is behind it
pointerEventsMode: Inherit: its own pointer style comes off
Explicit: the last Pointer Events Enabled is written back (on, before one was set)
pointerEventsEnabled: always, whatever the mode: off, the pointer passes through to what is behind it
draggable: always: on, every element it draws can be picked up, by pointer or keyboard; off, the one on the page cannot
dragValue: always: read by the zone it is dropped on, which reports it as Dropped Value
dragKind: always: read by a zone with an Accept Kind as it is dragged over one
holdToDrag: always: read at the next press — whether it must be held before it picks up
holdTime: always: read at the next held press — how many seconds it is held before it picks up
acceptDrops: on: a Draggable can be dropped here
off while a drag is over it: the drag leaves it — Is Drop Target goes false
off: nothing can be dropped here
acceptKind: always: read as a drag comes over it — a source of another kind does not light it up
acceptFileDrops: on: a file dragged from the desktop can be dropped here
off: no file can be dropped here, and a drag over it is forgotten — Is Dragging Over goes false if it was true
acceptedFileTypes: always: read at a drop — which files count as accepted
src: always: the picture drawn at the end of the frame — a project file, a URL, or nothing
srcSet: always: the sizes the browser may pick from instead, drawn at the end of the frame

dynamicPorts.description: This is the Function node. Input and output ports are discovered from the user script in the "functionScript" parameter, and the connectable port NAME carries a prefix the script does not: reading "Inputs.xyz" creates the input port "in-xyz", assigning "Outputs.xyz" creates the output port "out-xyz", and calling "Outputs.xyz()" creates the signal output "out-xyz". The property panel and the port list show the unprefixed display name ("xyz"), so connect to "in-xyz"/"out-xyz" — a connection written to the bare script name silently targets a port that does not exist. The node's own static ports ("run", "done", "success", "failure", "completed", "unchanged", "error") are never prefixed, so "Outputs.done()" is the separate port "out-done". The Script node ("Javascript2") does NOT prefix; that convention belongs to this node alone.

new code, with Run wired: compiled, and nothing runs until Run or a changed ticked input — a message on Error is cleared

run: always: one run at the end of the frame, however many Runs arrived — Success, and Done for each Run; Error, and Failure for each Run, if the code does not compile or throws; Unchanged for each Run when there is no code

states: always: the list of states; while none is current, the first (or Start State) is entered at the end of the frame
values: always: the values that differ between states, each an output; a value named as one of the node's outputs is refused and the editor is told
useTransitions: always: whether the next move animates its values or jumps
toggle: no States: refused, and Error says so → Failure
already in, or already heading to, the next state → Unchanged
otherwise it moves to the next state, wrapping round after the last, at the end of the frame — State Changed, then Done

warnings.states/unknown-state: a state was asked for that is not in the list, and no state in the list has been asked for since
warnings.states/no-states: a Toggle or a To arrived with no States list

warnings.states/reserved-port-name: a value is named as one of the node's own outputs

inputs.name: csv

inputs.name: json
inputs.description: An array of objects authored inline; unlike CSV it keeps numbers and booleans as they are — ignored unless Type is JSON

inputs.name: type
inputs.description: Which of the two authoring formats below is read

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: How many rows the last successful parse produced

outputs.name: error
outputs.description: Why the JSON could not be parsed, in one sentence; empty until a parse fails

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when the authored JSON could not be parsed, leaving Items as it was

outputs.name: items
outputs.description: The authored rows, as an array of records; unchanged while the JSON cannot be parsed

dynamicPorts.description: Output ports are derived from the columns/fields of the data entered in the "data" parameter.

declaredPortGroups.condition: type = csv OR type NOT SET

parameterEncoding.notes: This node computes no port names. Its dynamic behaviour is visibility only: every port it can ever have is listed in `inputs`/`outputs` above, and `dynamicPorts.declaredPortGroups` says which parameter values reveal which of them.

type: always: kept; the data is read again only when CSV or JSON changes
csv: always: the data is read again at the end of the frame, as Type says (CSV when unset) — Items and Count follow
json: always: the data is read again at the end of the frame, as Type says — Items and Count follow; with Type JSON, Error and Failure if it does not parse (Failure once per message)

inputs.name: runOnChange-value
inputs.description: Whether a new value on Value re-runs this node. On by default; untick to make this input passive so only the control signal runs it

inputs.name: saveValue
inputs.description: Stores the latest value now. This is additional to Value storing on change; untick Value under Run On Value Change to stop that

inputs.name: treatEmptyAs
inputs.description: Back-compat for graphs written before Variables were nullable. `null` (default) keeps a cleared value distinguishable from a real "". Choosing another option restores the pre-NDA-003 coercion for authors who relied on it.

inputs.name: treatUnchangedAs
inputs.description: What this node reports when the action was valid and there was nothing to do. Unchanged (the default) keeps it a third outcome of its own. Done suits a project whose chains should carry on either way. Completed fires whatever this is set to.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The empty-value contract (dev-docs/reference/EMPTY-VALUE-CONTRACT.md): `undefined` abstains and leaves the Variable's stored value untouched. `null` is a real value — it clears the Variable, is stored, and fires Changed. What "cleared" is stored as is controlled by `Treat empty as` (null by default).

outputs.name: changed
outputs.description: Fires whenever the stored value actually changed, however it was reached — including Value writing straight through under Run On Value Change. It is a value-level event, not the outcome of a Set

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires when a Set stored a value the Variable was not already holding

outputs.name: length
outputs.description: 0 when the Variable is cleared (`savedValue` is `null`) — there is no text to measure, and 0 is what an author reading this as a plain number expects, rather than a thrown error or `null` itself.

outputs.name: savedValue
outputs.description: Can be `null` — a cleared Variable (see `value`'s description) stores and emits null by default, not this type's zero value, unless `Treat empty as` says otherwise.

outputs.name: unchanged
outputs.description: Fires when a Set stored the value it already held, so nothing changed. ⚠️ With Value left ticked under Run On Value Change this is the common case, because Value has already stored by the time Set fires

value: undefined: ignored → Changed stays silent
the same as the last one, or Run On Value Change unticked: held for the next Set → Changed stays silent
a new value that converts to what is already stored: held, nothing changes → Changed stays silent
a new value, with Run On Value Change ticked: stored straight away (an empty one as Treat Empty As says) → Changed
saveValue: always: at the end of the frame the last Value is stored — Changed and Done if that changed it, otherwise Unchanged (or what Treat Unchanged As says)

ssr.note: A realtime subscription cannot be opened during a server render and would hold one connection per request; the node subscribes in the browser after hydration.

inputs.name: enabled
inputs.description: Hold the subscription open. Turn it off to stop receiving changes without deleting the node — the connection is closed and Subscribed goes false. On by default: this node has nothing else to do

outputs.name: changed
outputs.description: Any of the three, and also the backend saying the view may be stale after a reconnect — the one to react to if you do not care which happened

outputs.name: changedEvent
outputs.description: create, update, delete, init or resync

outputs.name: changedRecord
outputs.description: The record the change was about. ⚠️ Null on a delete against Directus, which sends only the key — use Changed Record Id, which every backend fills

outputs.name: changedRecordId
outputs.description: The id of the changed record, always a string — even where the backend's primary key is an integer

outputs.name: changedRecords
outputs.description: Every record in the change frame; some backends batch

outputs.name: created
outputs.description: Another client created a record in this collection

outputs.name: deleted
outputs.description: Another client deleted a record from this collection

outputs.name: realtimeError
outputs.description: The last realtime failure, with a code and whether retrying can help; null until one happens

outputs.name: realtimeFailure
outputs.description: Fires when a subscription cannot connect, is rejected, or has been given up on

outputs.name: realtimeStatus
outputs.description: connecting, subscribed, interrupted or stopped. Four states rather than a boolean, because "connecting for the first time" and "dropped and retrying" want different things on screen

outputs.name: subscribed
outputs.description: True while the backend has confirmed the subscription and is delivering changes

outputs.name: updated
outputs.description: Another client updated a record in this collection

dynamicPorts.description: Every input but "enabled" is discovered at runtime. "backendId" is a dropdown of the project's backends, defaulting to "_active_" and omitted entirely when the project has only one; "collectionName" is a dropdown of the selected backend's introspected classes; "visualFilter" is a query-filter editor built from that class's schema, and each filter value bound to a port mints one "qp-<name>" input. An authoring tool should set "collectionName" (and "backendId" only when the project has more than one backend); the outputs are all static.

parameterEncoding.reason: No parameter on this node carries the list its ports are generated from, so the port set could not be observed headlessly.

enabled: a change (on is anything truthy): at the frame's end the subscription held is closed — Subscribed and Realtime Status sent when one was held — and, on, with a Class and a Backend the project has, a new one is opened: Realtime Status is connecting, then whatever the backend tells
the value it already holds: nothing — the subscription stays as it is

inputs.name: end

string: always: read as text (null counts as empty); Result follows

inputs.name: flip
inputs.description: Switches to whichever state it is not currently in

inputs.name: off
inputs.description: Switches off, or fires Unchanged if it is already off

inputs.name: on
inputs.description: Switches on, or fires Unchanged if it is already on

inputs.name: onFromStart
inputs.description: State to start in, and setting it announces a switch on Switched even though nothing switched

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires when the switch actually changed state

outputs.name: state
outputs.description: True while the switch is on — wire it into a mounted or visible port for a gate that turns on AND off

outputs.name: switched
outputs.description: Fires on every state change, alongside whichever of Switched To On and Switched To Off applies

outputs.name: switchedToOff
outputs.description: Fires when the switch becomes off

outputs.name: switchedToOn
outputs.description: Fires when the switch becomes on

outputs.name: unchanged
outputs.description: Fires when it was already in that state, so none of the Switched signals fired

on: already on → Unchanged; Switched To On, Switched stay silent
while off: it switches on → Switched To On, Switched, Done
off: while on: it switches off → Switched To Off, Switched, Done
already off → Unchanged; Switched To Off, Switched stay silent
flip: while on: it switches off → Switched To Off, Switched, Done; Switched To On stays silent
while off: it switches on → Switched To On, Switched, Done; Switched To Off stays silent
onFromStart: true: the switch is on, announced even if it already was → Switched To On, Switched; Switched To Off stays silent
false: the switch is off, announced even if it already was → Switched To Off, Switched; Switched To On stays silent

inputs.description: Begins the countdown again from zero, whether or not one is already running

inputs.description: Abandons the countdown, so Finished never fires for it

outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.description: Fires once Duration has elapsed, and not at all for a countdown that was stopped

outputs.description: Fires on a Start while one is already running, or a Stop with nothing running

start: a countdown running: nothing — Restart begins one again → Unchanged
otherwise (a Start earlier this frame included): the countdown is queued, and begins at the frame's end, Start Delay later — Started fires then → Done
restart: always: a running countdown is dropped without Finished, and a new one is queued from zero for the frame's end → Done
stop: a countdown running or queued: it is dropped, and Finished never fires for it → Done

parameterEncoding.reason: No parameter on this node carries the list its ports are generated from, so the port set could not be observed headlessly.

private: always: held as handed; read when the next Upload goes
bucket: always: held as handed; read when the next Upload goes — set, the file goes to this bucket at Path (or under the file's own name)

dynamicPorts.description: Declares conditional/expandable port groups whose visibility depends on parameter values (see declaredPortGroups).

declaredPortGroups.condition: borderStyle = solid OR borderStyle = dashed OR borderStyle = dotted
borderLeftStyle = solid OR borderLeftStyle = dashed OR borderLeftStyle = dotted OR borderStyle = solid OR borderStyle = dashed OR borderStyle = dotted
borderTopStyle = solid OR borderTopStyle = dashed OR borderTopStyle = dotted OR borderStyle = solid OR borderStyle = dashed OR borderStyle = dotted
borderRightStyle = solid OR borderRightStyle = dashed OR borderRightStyle = dotted OR borderStyle = solid OR borderStyle = dashed OR borderStyle = dotted
borderBottomStyle = solid OR borderBottomStyle = dashed OR borderBottomStyle = dotted OR borderStyle = solid OR borderStyle = dashed OR borderStyle = dotted

accept.rule: a data attribute name: "data-", then a lowercase letter or digit, then lowercase letters, digits, ".", "_" or "-"

variables.name: one of the names listed in the `dataAttributes` parameter; a data attribute name: "data-", then a lowercase letter or digit, then lowercase letters, digits, ".", "_" or "-"

parameterEncoding.notes: Every port is listed in `inputs`/`outputs` above except the ones named by a list parameter (the patterns here): `dynamicPorts.declaredPortGroups` says which parameter values reveal which listed port, and holds the `namedports/derived` rule that turns each listed name into a port.

mounted: a change: the element is put on the page, or taken off it, at the next paint
the value it already holds: nothing
scrollIntoView: always: the page, or the scrolling Group holding it, scrolls until the element can be seen
visible: always: shown or hidden at the next paint, its space kept; hidden, it takes no pointer
opacity: always: how see-through it is; at exactly 0 it takes no pointer, and an act goes to what is behind it
pointerEventsMode: Inherit: its own pointer style comes off
Explicit: the last Pointer Events Enabled is written back (on, before one was set)
pointerEventsEnabled: always, whatever the mode: off, the pointer passes through to what is behind it
draggable: always: on, every element it draws can be picked up, by pointer or keyboard; off, the one on the page cannot
dragValue: always: read by the zone it is dropped on, which reports it as Dropped Value
dragKind: always: read by a zone with an Accept Kind as it is dragged over one
holdToDrag: always: read at the next press — whether it must be held before it picks up
holdTime: always: read at the next held press — how many seconds it is held before it picks up
acceptDrops: on: a Draggable can be dropped here
off while a drag is over it: the drag leaves it — Is Drop Target goes false
off: nothing can be dropped here
acceptKind: always: read as a drag comes over it — a source of another kind does not light it up
acceptFileDrops: on: a file dragged from the desktop can be dropped here
off: no file can be dropped here, and a drag over it is forgotten — Is Dragging Over goes false if it was true
acceptedFileTypes: always: read at a drop — which files count as accepted
src: always: what is drawn at the end of the frame — a project file or a URL as a video, a YouTube or Vimeo link in an embedded player, or nothing; a different file loads afresh, paused and back at the start
startTime: always: where the video begins, put into the address it loads from (blank: the start; below 0 is 0); a change that moves it loads the video again at the next paint, paused
endTime: always: where the first play-through stops, put into the address with Start Time (ignored unless later than Start Time; approximate on YouTube, ignored on Vimeo); a change that moves it loads the video again at the next paint, paused
muted: always: drawn at the next paint — on, the video is silent, and Play or Autoplay may start it before a person has pressed, clicked or typed on the page
autoplay: always: drawn at the next paint, and read as a load completes — on, a video that may play (Muted, or a person has acted on the page) and that Pause or Reset has not stopped since the load began starts by itself: On Can Play, then On Play
loop: always: drawn at the next paint, and read as the video reaches its end — on, it goes back to the start and plays on; off, it pauses there (On Pause)
srcObject: off the page: waits for the element behind the actions already waiting, in order, and is written at the paint that puts the video there (at most 16 wait, and the oldest is pushed out)
null (what it already has), a value that is not a stream, or anything on an embedded player: nothing changes — a live stream itself plays in place of Source, and no scenario holds one

nothing (undefined) on a video: the browser is handed null, so it loads Source again — paused, back at the start (Playback Position 0 when it had moved) — and Play waits for the new On Can Play before it can start it
play: on the page: wants the video playing and, once it has loaded, starts it — On Play if it was paused (from the start again after its end); Error then Playback Failure if the browser refuses (not Muted and no person has acted on the page) or the load failed; an embedded player is not reached — Done, in its turn after outcomes the frame has already resolved
off the page: waits for the element (at most 16 wait, and the oldest pushed out reports Failure) and plays at the paint that puts the video there — Done then
restart: on the page: wants the video playing and, once it has loaded, goes back to Start Time as last drawn (Playback Position; second 0 when there is none) and starts it as Play does; before the load, only the wanting; an embedded player is not reached — Done, in its turn after outcomes the frame has already resolved
off the page: waits for the element (at most 16 wait, and the oldest pushed out reports Failure) and restarts at the paint that puts the video there — Done then
pause: on the page: stops wanting the video playing, and pauses one that is playing — Playback Position, then On Pause; one already paused stays so; Autoplay no longer starts it on this load; an embedded player is not reached — Done, in its turn after outcomes the frame has already resolved
off the page: waits for the element (at most 16 wait, and the oldest pushed out reports Failure) and pauses at the paint that puts the video there — Done then
reset: on the page: stops wanting the video playing, goes back to Start Time as last drawn (Playback Position, once loaded; second 0 when there is none) and pauses it — On Pause if it was playing; Autoplay no longer starts it on this load; an embedded player is not reached — Done, in its turn after outcomes the frame has already resolved
off the page: waits for the element (at most 16 wait, and the oldest pushed out reports Failure) and resets at the paint that puts the video there — Done then

fetch: always: one request at the frame's end, however many Fetches arrived, with the values held then, beside any request already running: a 2xx answer sends Response, Status Code and Response Headers, then Done for each Fetch; any other status the same and Error, then Failure; a 304 is Not Modified and Unchanged; no URL, an input that is not text, a body that is not JSON, no answer by Timeout (ms) or none at all is Error and Failure

outputs.name: values
outputs.description: Every value completed by the most recent Parse, in order

chunk: always: kept as text (nothing as empty) for the next Parse, and retained after it — a second Parse appends it again
format: always: read at the next Parse — one value per line, any run of complete values, or one whole document (empty reads as NDJSON; anything else as Stream)
maxLength: always: read at the next Parse — the pending text a Parse gives up on when longer (not above 0: no cap)
parse: nothing pending and an empty Chunk: nothing to read → Unchanged; Success stays silent

the Chunk appended makes the pending text longer than Max Pending: all of it is dropped unread, the reason on Error, Error Count grows — Pending Characters and Is Complete are not re-sent → Failure; Success stays silent

some values came out complete and something would not parse (a bad line, or a value that scans whole but is not JSON): the values are on Values and Parsed, the last reason on Error, Error Count grows by each — the Parse still fails → Success, Failure
at least one value came out complete and nothing failed: Values holds them, Parsed the last, Value Count grows; what is left waits as Pending Characters → Success, Done
nothing came out complete and something would not parse: the last reason on Error, Error Count grows by each → Failure; Success stays silent
no value is complete yet and nothing failed: the text waits as Pending Characters, Is Complete false → Done; Success stays silent
clear: anything pending, parsed or failed: the pending text, Values, both counts and the Error are emptied — Parsed keeps its last value on the wire, and the Chunk is retained → Cleared, Done
nothing held: the same empty values are sent again → Cleared, Unchanged

inputs.name: data
inputs.description: An optional object written alongside the message as structured fields. In a cloud function every property whose NAME says it holds a credential is redacted on the way out

inputs.name: level
inputs.description: How loud this line is. In a cloud function the backend drops anything below its configured level, so Debug lines cost nothing in production unless someone turns them on

inputs.name: log
inputs.description: Writes the line. Nothing is written until this fires

inputs.name: message
inputs.description: The line to write. Free text, so keep credentials out of it by habit — the backend does scrub the values of its own stored secrets out of this before it is written, but that cannot cover a credential it never issued

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Passed straight through to the Value output, so this node can sit inline on a wire

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation. This node has no other outcome — no Unchanged and no Failure — so it always fires together with Done, and wiring either one does the same thing. It is here on every action so that reaching for it is never a per-node decision

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires once the line has been written

outputs.name: value
outputs.description: Whatever arrived on the Value input, unchanged — this node never alters what passes through it

value: always: passed straight through to Value; nothing is written
log: always: the line is written now, from Message, Level and Data as they stand → Done

inputs.name: read
inputs.description: Re-reads the clock. The outputs hold the instant of the last Read, not a live value

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation. This node has no other outcome — no Unchanged and no Failure — so it always fires together with Done, and wiring either one does the same thing. It is here on every action so that reaching for it is never a per-node decision

outputs.name: date
outputs.description: The instant of the last Read, for the other date nodes

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires once the outputs hold the freshly-read instant

outputs.name: iso
outputs.description: The same instant as an ISO-8601 string in UTC — the shape to put in a JSON body

outputs.name: timestamp
outputs.description: The same instant as milliseconds since 1 January 1970 UTC

read: always: the clock is read, and Date, Timestamp and ISO String all say that moment → Done

inputs.name: object
inputs.description: The Object to watch. Changes to its keys are reported as they happen; sending a different Object reports Object Replaced. A plain JavaScript object that is not a Noodl Object cannot be watched key-by-key — only its replacement is reported

outputs.name: key
outputs.description: The key the last Key Added or Key Changed was about; empty after Object Replaced, which is about no single key

outputs.name: keyAdded
outputs.description: Fires when a key that did not exist on the watched Object now does

outputs.name: keyChanged
outputs.description: Fires when a key that already existed on the watched Object is given a different value

outputs.name: objectReplaced
outputs.description: Fires when a different Object arrives on the input, including the first one and including an explicit clear; Key is empty and Value / Previous Value carry the Objects themselves

outputs.name: previousValue
outputs.description: The value that key held before — empty when the key has just been added — or, after Object Replaced, the Object that was being watched before

outputs.name: value
outputs.description: The new value of that key — or, after Object Replaced, the Object that just arrived

inputs.name: apply
inputs.description: Writes Optimistic Value at Key now and opens a transaction the server response will resolve

inputs.name: commit
inputs.description: Confirms the update, so the optimistic value becomes the truth

inputs.name: errorMessage
inputs.description: Reason reported on Error when this update is rolled back; wire the server error here

inputs.name: key
inputs.description: Key to write optimistically; an Apply with no key is refused rather than dropped

inputs.name: onDispose
inputs.description: What happens to updates still in flight when this node is removed: put the old value back, or keep the value that was shown

inputs.name: optimisticValue
inputs.description: Value to show immediately, before the server has confirmed anything

inputs.name: rollback
inputs.description: Puts the old value back, unless something else has written the key since

inputs.name: storeName
inputs.description: Names the store holding the key this update writes

inputs.name: timeout
inputs.description: Milliseconds to wait for an answer before rolling back on its own; 0 waits forever

inputs.name: transactionId
inputs.description: Names the update to commit or roll back when several are in flight; leave blank to generate one and resolve to the oldest

outputs.name: applied
outputs.description: Fires once the optimistic value is in the store and the transaction is open

outputs.name: committed
outputs.description: Fires once an update has been confirmed and its value is the truth

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires when the action did its work: an Apply that opened a transaction, a Commit that confirmed one, or a Rollback that put the old value back

outputs.name: error
outputs.description: Why the last update failed or was undone; blank once an Apply succeeds

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when the node refused to act: no Key, a transaction id already open, or no such update to resolve

outputs.name: isCommitted
outputs.description: True when the last update to resolve was confirmed

outputs.name: isPending
outputs.description: True while at least one update is waiting for an answer

outputs.name: isRolledBack
outputs.description: True when the last update to resolve was undone, whether by Rollback, by the deadline, or by disposal

outputs.name: pendingCount
outputs.description: How many updates are open at once, which can be more than one when responses come back out of order

outputs.name: previousValue
outputs.description: What the key held immediately before the most recent Apply; blank when the key did not exist

outputs.name: rolledBack
outputs.description: Fires once an update has been undone, including when the value was left alone because something newer had written the key

outputs.name: timedOut
outputs.description: Fires alongside Rolled Back when it was the deadline rather than the graph that ended the update

outputs.name: transactionId
outputs.description: Id of the most recent Apply; carry it through the request and hand it back to resolve that update specifically

outputs.name: unchanged
outputs.description: Fires when a Rollback resolved its transaction without restoring anything, because something else had already written the key — the value this update wrote was gone already, so there was nothing to undo. Rolled Back fires too, and Error says why

outputs.name: value
outputs.description: What the key holds right now, following writes made by anything, not only by this node

inputs.name: fetch
inputs.description: Republishes every property from the parent now. This is additional to the outputs updating on their own; untick Parent object under Run On Value Change to stop that

inputs.name: properties
inputs.description: Names of the parent values to expose, each becoming a matching input and output

inputs.name: runOnChange-object
inputs.description: Whether a new value on Parent object re-runs this node. On by default; untick to make this input passive so only the control signal runs it

inputs.name: targetComponent
inputs.description: Which ancestor to read from; leave blank for the nearest one that has a Component Object

outputs.name: changed
outputs.description: Fires when a property on the resolved parent is written, unless Fetch is connected

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires once a Fetch you triggered has republished every property, after Fetched

outputs.name: error
outputs.description: Which ancestor was looked for and why it was not found

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when no parent Component Object could be found, so there is nothing to read

outputs.name: fetched
outputs.description: Fires whenever every property is republished, whether by Fetch or by the parent being re-resolved

dynamicPorts.description: Property ports mirror the parent component object's property schema.

variables.property: one of the comma-separated entries in the `properties` parameter
one of the comma-separated entries in the `properties` parameter

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: The character between cells. Use ; for a European export, or a tab for TSV

inputs.name: hasHeader
inputs.description: When ticked the first row names the columns and Items is an array of records. Untick it and Items is an array of rows, each an array of cells

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The CSV text to parse. A leading byte-order mark — which is what Excel writes when it saves UTF-8 — is stripped, so the first column keeps its name

outputs.name: changed
outputs.description: Fires once Items and Count hold the freshly parsed CSV

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: How many rows the last successful parse produced, not counting the header row

outputs.name: error
outputs.description: Why the CSV could not be parsed, naming the line it gave up on; empty until a parse fails

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when the CSV could not be parsed, leaving Items and Count as they were

outputs.name: items
outputs.description: The parsed rows — records when Has Header is ticked, arrays of cells when it is not. Every cell is a string, including columns that look numeric. Unchanged while the CSV cannot be parsed

text: always: parsed at the end of the frame (once, however many inputs moved) — Items, Count and Changed, or Error and Failure with Items and Count untouched; nothing (undefined or null) is not parsed, a number parses as its text
hasHeader: always: the CSV is parsed again at the end of the frame, once any has arrived — the first row names the columns and Items holds records in a fresh array, or Items holds the rows as arrays of cells
delimiter: always: the CSV is parsed again at the end of the frame, once any has arrived, split on this (cleared reads as a comma)

inputs.name: maxBytes
inputs.description: Refuse a document longer than this many characters (not bytes), before parsing it. Raise it for a source that really does publish its whole archive in one file

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The feed document — RSS 2.0, Atom 1.0 or RDF/RSS 1.0. Wire an HTTP Request node's Response here with its Response Type set to Text: feeds are served as application/rss+xml, text/xml and, from some sources, text/html, and Text is what guarantees the body arrives untouched

outputs.name: changed
outputs.description: Fires once Items and the Feed outputs hold the freshly parsed feed

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: How many items Items holds after the last successful parse

outputs.name: error
outputs.description: Why the feed could not be read; empty until a parse fails

outputs.name: errorCode
outputs.description: A stable code for the failure, for a graph that branches rather than reads: feed/unrecognised when the document is XML but not a feed, otherwise the Parse XML codes (xml/too-large, xml/entity-declaration, xml/doctype-subset, xml/parse-failed, xml/empty)

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when the feed could not be read, leaving Items and Count as they were

outputs.name: feedDescription
outputs.description: The feed's description, or an Atom feed's subtitle

outputs.name: feedLink
outputs.description: The site the feed belongs to — its alternate link, never its own XML address

outputs.name: feedTitle
outputs.description: The title of the feed itself, not of any item

outputs.name: feedUpdated
outputs.description: When the feed last changed, as an ISO 8601 string; empty when it did not say

outputs.name: items
outputs.description: The feed's items, always an array whether the feed carried one or a hundred. Each has Id, Title, Link, Published, Updated, Author, Summary, Content, Image, Enclosure, Tags and Raw. Id is never empty — it is the guid, or the Atom id, or the link, or a hash of title and date — which is what lets a collection store each item once. Each item is the app's shared record of its Id: two items with one Id are one record, with the later item's fields, and an Object node or another Parse Feed using that Id holds the same one. Unchanged while the feed cannot be parsed

outputs.name: kind
outputs.description: Which format this was: rss, atom or rdf

outputs.name: source
outputs.description: A hint at where the feed came from, for a graph that wants to branch: youtube, reddit, podcast or generic. A hint, not a promise — generic is what an unrecognised source gets and it is not a failure

text: always: parsed at the end of the frame (once, however many inputs moved) — Items in a fresh array, Count, the six Feed outputs and Changed, or Error, Error Code and Failure with everything else untouched; nothing (undefined or null) is not parsed
maxBytes: always: the Feed is parsed again at the end of the frame, once any has arrived — a text longer than this (counted in characters) is refused as xml/too-large before parsing; not a finite number above 0 reads as the default, 5 MB

inputs.name: alwaysArray
inputs.description: Comma-separated tag names that are always an array, however many times they appear. Without this, a document with one <item> and a document with ten have different shapes and everything downstream needs a branch

inputs.name: attributePrefix
inputs.description: What an attribute's key starts with, so it cannot collide with a child element of the same name. With the default, <a href="x"/> is { "@href": "x" }

inputs.name: maxBytes
inputs.description: Refuse a document longer than this many characters (not bytes), before parsing it. A big document costs many times its own size in memory once it is an object, and a server can always send more than you expected

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The XML text to parse. Wire an HTTP Request node's Response here with its Response Type set to Text, so the body reaches this node untouched whatever content-type the server claimed

inputs.name: trimValues
inputs.description: Strip leading and trailing whitespace from text. Untick it to keep a document's indentation

outputs.name: changed
outputs.description: Fires once Result holds the freshly parsed document

outputs.name: error
outputs.description: Why the XML could not be read; empty until a parse fails

outputs.name: errorCode
outputs.description: A stable code for the failure, for a graph that branches rather than reads: xml/too-large, xml/entity-declaration, xml/doctype-subset, xml/parse-failed, xml/empty

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when the XML could not be parsed or was refused, leaving Result as it was

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: The document as an object. Every value is a string, including ones that look numeric — an id of 0123 stays "0123". A tag carrying both attributes and text becomes { "@attr": "…", "#text": "…" }. Unchanged while the XML cannot be parsed

text: always: parsed at the end of the frame (once, however many inputs moved) — Result and Changed, or Error, Error Code and Failure with Result untouched; nothing (undefined or null) is not parsed
attributePrefix: always: the XML is parsed again at the end of the frame, once any has arrived, with attribute keys starting with this (nothing reads as @; empty is a real prefix: the bare name)
alwaysArray: always: read as text — the XML is parsed again at the end of the frame, once any has arrived, with these comma-separated tags always arrays
trimValues: always: the XML is parsed again at the end of the frame, once any has arrived, with text values trimmed or kept as written
maxBytes: always: the XML is parsed again at the end of the frame, once any has arrived — a text longer than this (counted in characters) is refused as xml/too-large before parsing; not a finite number above 0 reads as the default, 5 MB

inputs.name: extract
inputs.description: Runs Pattern over Text and reports what it found

inputs.name: extractAll
inputs.description: Collects every match into Matches instead of stopping at the first one

inputs.name: flags
inputs.description: Regex flags i, m, s, u and y; g is controlled by Extract All and a g written here is ignored

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.description: A JavaScript regular expression without the surrounding slashes; capture groups appear on Groups

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text to search

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires once the extract has run, whether it matched or not — Found and Not Found say which

outputs.name: error
outputs.description: Why the pattern could not be used: it is blank, or it is not a valid regular expression

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when the pattern itself is unusable, which is a bug to fix rather than a result

outputs.name: firstGroup
outputs.description: The first capture group of the first match, which is the whole answer for a pattern like (\d+)%

outputs.name: found
outputs.description: Fires when the pattern ran and matched at least once

outputs.name: groups
outputs.description: Capture groups of the first match; an optional group that did not participate is a blank string, not a hole

outputs.name: match
outputs.description: The first match, or blank when nothing matched

outputs.name: matchCount
outputs.description: How many matches were found, which is at most one unless Extract All is on

outputs.name: matches
outputs.description: Every match when Extract All is on, otherwise just the first

outputs.name: namedGroups
outputs.description: Named capture groups of the first match, keyed by name

outputs.name: notFound
outputs.description: Fires when the pattern ran and matched nothing, which is an ordinary outcome rather than a mistake

text: always: kept as text (nothing as empty) and read at the next Extract
pattern: always: kept as text (nothing as empty) and read at the next Extract — a regular expression without its slashes
flags: always: kept as text (nothing as empty) and read at the next Extract — only i, m, s, u and y count; g comes from Extract All
extractAll: always: read at the next Extract — every match into Matches, or only the first
extract: a blank Pattern, or one that is not a valid regular expression: every output is rewritten empty and Error says why → Failure; Not Found, Found stay silent
the Pattern ran and matched nothing (empty Text matches nothing): every output is rewritten empty, Error cleared — an ordinary result → Not Found, Done; Found stays silent
the Pattern ran and matched: Match, Matches, Groups, First Group, Named Groups and Match Count are rewritten, Error cleared → Found, Done; Not Found stays silent

inputs.name: encoding
inputs.description: How the bytes are rendered as text. Base64 URL is the safe one for a URL or a token

inputs.name: generate
inputs.description: Generates a fresh block of random bytes

inputs.name: length
inputs.description: How many random BYTES to generate (not characters — hex renders each byte as two). 1 to 4096

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires once fresh random bytes are available on Value

outputs.name: error
outputs.description: Why no random bytes were produced

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when there is no cryptographic random source here, or Length is out of range. This node will not quietly substitute Math.random()

outputs.name: value
outputs.description: The random bytes rendered in Encoding, replaced on every New

generate: Length not a whole number from 1 to 4096: nothing is drawn, the reason on Error, Value untouched → Failure
an Encoding not in the list (empty reads as hex): Length bytes were drawn and are thrown away, the reason on Error, Value untouched → Failure
Length bytes are drawn from the cryptographic source and rendered in Encoding: Value replaced, Error cleared → Done

ssr.note: An event stream cannot be consumed during a server render; the node connects in the browser after hydration.

inputs.name: autoConnect
inputs.description: Opens the stream as soon as a URL is available, without waiting for a Connect signal

inputs.name: autoReconnect
inputs.description: Retries after a failure with a growing backoff; turning it off reports the failure and stops

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: Request body, sent as JSON unless it is already a string; ignored for GET and HEAD

inputs.name: connect
inputs.description: Opens the stream, replacing any connection already open and resetting the retry count

inputs.name: dedupeById
inputs.description: Drops events whose id has already been seen, so a reconnect that resumes cannot re-deliver messages

inputs.name: disconnect
inputs.description: Closes the stream and stops retrying

inputs.name: eventTypes
inputs.description: Comma-separated named event types to subscribe to; only needed for the EventSource transport, as Fetch delivers every type

inputs.name: headers
inputs.description: Request headers as an object, for bearer tokens and the like; ignored by the EventSource transport, which cannot set them

inputs.name: maxReconnectDelay
inputs.description: Ceiling on the backoff in milliseconds, however many failures there have been

inputs.name: maxRetries
inputs.description: Consecutive failures allowed before the connection gives up and reports an error; 0 keeps retrying

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: HTTP method for the request; anything other than GET needs the Fetch transport

inputs.name: reconnectDelay
inputs.description: First retry delay in milliseconds, doubling per consecutive failure up to Max Reconnect Delay

inputs.name: reconnectOnStreamEnd
inputs.description: Reconnects when the server closes the stream cleanly; off by default because reconnecting an agent stream re-issues the request

inputs.name: textPath
inputs.description: Where the text lives inside a JSON payload, as a dot path such as choices.0.delta.content; leave blank for a stream of bare text

inputs.name: transport
inputs.description: How the stream is fetched: Fetch carries headers and a body, EventSource lets the browser handle reconnection, Auto prefers Fetch

inputs.name: url
inputs.description: Endpoint to stream from; changing it while connected reconnects to the new one

inputs.name: withCredentials
inputs.description: Sends cookies and HTTP auth to a cross-origin endpoint, which the server must also allow

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: connected
outputs.description: True only while the stream is open and frames may arrive

outputs.name: connectionState
outputs.description: Where the connection is: idle, connecting, open, reconnecting, closed or error

outputs.name: data
outputs.description: The event payload, parsed as JSON when it is JSON and handed over as text when it is not

outputs.name: deliverySemantics
outputs.description: What this stream actually guarantees, derived from whether the server sends ids: at-most-once, at-least-once or at-least-once-deduped

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires when the action finished: a Connect whose stream opened, or a Disconnect that stopped one

outputs.name: duplicatesSuppressed
outputs.description: How many replayed events Dedupe By Id has dropped on this connection

outputs.name: eventType
outputs.description: The event name the server sent, or message when it sent none

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when the stream could not be opened, or gave up retrying. Last Error carries the reason

outputs.name: lastError
outputs.description: What went wrong most recently, including the reason a retry was scheduled

outputs.name: lastEventId
outputs.description: The furthest id the server has reported, which is the point a reconnect resumes from

outputs.name: lastMessageTime
outputs.description: When the last event arrived, as milliseconds since the epoch; useful for spotting a stalled stream

outputs.name: messageCount
outputs.description: How many events have been delivered on this connection, not counting suppressed duplicates

outputs.name: onClose
outputs.description: Fires when the stream has stopped for good, whether it ended cleanly or gave up

outputs.name: onError
outputs.description: Fires when the stream failed or dropped, whether or not a retry is going to follow

outputs.name: onMessage
outputs.description: Fires once per event, after Data, Raw and Text already hold it

outputs.name: onOpen
outputs.description: Fires when the stream has been established

outputs.name: raw
outputs.description: The event payload exactly as it arrived, before any parsing

outputs.name: retryCount
outputs.description: Consecutive failed attempts in the current outage; back to zero once the stream opens

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The one data output guaranteed to be a string: Raw when no Text Path is set, the field at that path when one is, blank when it does not resolve

outputs.name: unchanged
outputs.description: Fires when there was nothing to do: a Disconnect with no stream running, or a Connect a later Connect or Disconnect superseded before it opened

url: always: stored as text (nothing as empty); at the end of the frame a stream opened against another URL is dropped silently (a Connect still waiting: Unchanged) and reopened to this one when Auto Connect is on and it is not blank, else said idle (Connection State, Connected, Retry Count); with no stream, Auto Connect on and a URL: it connects; the URL the stream was opened against: left alone
autoConnect: always: on or off, read at the end of the frame — on with a URL and no stream: it connects; a stream opened against another URL is dropped silently (a Connect still waiting: Unchanged) and reopened when on, said idle when off; a stream on the URL it holds is left alone either way, so off never closes one
transport: always: read by the next connection, not one already open (nothing as Auto) — Auto and Fetch make a streaming request that carries Method, Headers and Body; EventSource asks the browser for one, which carries none of them and listens for Event Types, and where there is none that Connect fails for good (Last Error `EventSource is not available in this environment`)
method: always: read by the next connection, not one already open — the request's method, upper-cased (nothing as GET); with GET the Body stays home
headers: always: read by the next connection, not one already open — an object's entries go on the request as text after Accept and Cache-Control (a null or undefined one skipped), and a content-type among them, any case, keeps the JSON one off; anything else: none; the EventSource transport carries none
body: always: read by the next connection, not one already open — with a Method other than GET or HEAD a string goes as itself, anything else as JSON with Content-Type application/json unless Headers names one; nothing, or GET: no body; the EventSource transport carries none
withCredentials: always: read by the next connection, not one already open — on, the request carries cookies and HTTP auth across origins (credentials include); off, same-origin only
eventTypes: always: read by the next connection, not one already open, as text (nothing as none) split on commas and trimmed — the named events the EventSource transport listens for beside message; the Fetch transport delivers every type whatever is here
autoReconnect: always: read by the next connection, not one already open — on, a failure that can be retried (the server unreachable, a 5xx, 408 or 429, a stream cut short) schedules a reconnect; off, it is reported and the stream stops: Last Error, On Error, Connection State error, On Close
reconnectOnStreamEnd: always: read by the next connection, not one already open — on, a stream the server ends cleanly is reopened after the backoff wait, no error told and the retry count unmoved; off, it is closed (Connection State closed, On Close); either way a last event the server did not finish with a blank line is delivered first
reconnectDelay: always: read by the next connection, not one already open — the first retry's wait in milliseconds, doubled per consecutive failure after the first and capped at Max Reconnect Delay; a `retry:` the server sends replaces it for the rest of that connection; 0, below, or not a number: 1000
maxReconnectDelay: always: read by the next connection, not one already open — the ceiling on the retry wait in milliseconds, however many failures in a row; 0, below, or not a number: 30000
maxRetries: always: read by the next connection, not one already open — above 0, that many retries are made and the failure after the last gives up: Last Error `… (gave up after n attempts)`, On Error again, Connection State error, On Close, a waiting Connect Failure; 0, below, or not a number: it retries for as long as Auto Reconnect is on
dedupeById: always: read by the next connection, not one already open — on, an event whose id is among the last 512 seen on that connection is dropped: Duplicates Suppressed counts it (sent) and nothing else is told, though the resume point moves to it; off, every event is delivered and Delivery Semantics says at-least-once once ids are seen
textPath: always: stored as text (nothing as empty) and Text is sent at once, re-read from the last event — the field at this dot path in Data when it is a string, number or boolean, Raw when the path is blank, empty when it does not resolve
connect: no URL: a stream already open or retrying is dropped silently (its request abandoned, its timer cancelled; a Connect still waiting: Unchanged), then it fails for good — Last Error `No URL was set on the stream`, On Error, Connection State error (Connected false, Retry Count 0), On Close; Failure (sse/connect-failed)

Transport EventSource: the old stream dropped silently (a Connect still waiting: Unchanged), Retry Count 0, Last Error cleared, Connection State connecting, then the browser's EventSource is asked for — none here, so it fails for good: Last Error `EventSource is not available in this environment`, On Error, Connection State error, On Close; Failure (sse/connect-failed)

otherwise: the old stream dropped silently (its request abandoned, its timer cancelled; a Connect still waiting: Unchanged), Retry Count 0, Last Error cleared, Connection State connecting (Connected false), and a fresh request goes out — Method, Headers, Body, no Last-Event-ID (only a reconnect resumes); the answer settles it later: Connection State open, Last Error, On Open and Done at a 2xx with a body, else a failure (retried with Auto Reconnect unless it is a 4xx other than 408 and 429)
disconnect: no connection (none made yet, or the last dropped by a URL change): nothing is sent; Unchanged

a stream open, connecting or waiting to retry: its request is abandoned and its timer cancelled, nothing more arrives, Connection State closed (Connected false), On Close; a Connect still waiting: Unchanged; Done
a connection that already failed for good: it is marked closed — Connection State closed, Connected, Retry Count, and On Close once more; Unchanged
a connection already closed: nothing is sent; Unchanged

outputs.name: completed

outputs.name: currentIndex

outputs.name: done

outputs.name: fullyRestorable

outputs.name: historyChanged

outputs.name: historySize

outputs.name: unchanged

inputs.name: jumpTo

inputs.name: storeName

outputs.name: byReferenceKeys

outputs.name: completed

outputs.name: fullyRestorable
