ssr.note: Interval-based flushing needs a running timer, so it only happens in the browser. Add, Flush and size-based flushing behave normally.

inputs.name: add
inputs.description: Buffers the current Data, flushing straight away if that reaches Flush Size

inputs.name: clear
inputs.description: Discards the buffer and resets both counters without flushing

inputs.name: data
inputs.description: The next item to buffer, of any type; its value is retained between pulses of Add

inputs.name: flush
inputs.description: Hands the whole buffer to Flushed Data now; an empty buffer is a legitimate no-op

inputs.name: flushInterval
inputs.description: Flush automatically this often in milliseconds while items are buffered; 0 disables interval flushing

inputs.name: flushSize
inputs.description: Flush automatically once this many items are buffered; 0 disables size-based flushing

inputs.name: maxSize
inputs.description: Hard cap on buffered items; overflow drops the oldest and is counted on Dropped Items; 0 means no cap

outputs.name: buffer
outputs.description: Items waiting to be flushed, oldest first

outputs.name: bufferSize
outputs.description: How many items are waiting, which is what Flush Size is compared against

outputs.name: cleared
outputs.description: Fires once the buffer has been discarded

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires once an Add, Flush or Clear you triggered has changed the buffer

outputs.name: droppedItems
outputs.description: How many items Max Size has discarded from the front since the last Clear

outputs.name: error
outputs.description: Why the last Add was refused; blank until one is

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when Add ran before any value had arrived on Data, so nothing was buffered

outputs.name: flushCount
outputs.description: How many flushes have happened since the last Clear

outputs.name: flushed
outputs.description: Fires once Flushed Data holds a new batch, and not for a flush that found nothing

outputs.name: flushedData
outputs.description: The batch handed over by the most recent flush; a stable array that later Adds do not mutate

outputs.name: overflowed
outputs.description: Fires when Max Size has just discarded something

outputs.name: unchanged
outputs.description: Fires when a Flush found nothing to send, or a Clear found nothing to discard — an idle buffer doing exactly what it should

data: always: kept as it came for the next Add, and retained after it — any write counts as data having arrived, nothing included
flushSize: always: read at the next Add — the size at which that Add flushes (not above 0: never by size); a buffer already that big waits for an Add
maxSize: always: read at the next Add — the cap past which the oldest are dropped (not at least 0: 0, no cap); a buffer already over it is trimmed by the next Add
flushInterval: the period it already holds (not above 0 reads as 0): nothing
a different period above 0 with anything buffered: a running timer stops and a new one starts, to flush after the new period
a different period with nothing buffered, or 0 (never by time): a running timer stops; a period above 0 is armed by the next Add
add: before anything has arrived on Data: refused — the reason on Error, which nothing later clears → Failure; Overflowed, Flushed stay silent

Data joins, past Max Size the oldest go (counted on Dropped Items), and the buffer reaches Flush Size: it becomes Flushed Data, a fresh one starts, Flush Count grows, a running timer stops → Overflowed, Flushed, Done

Data joins, past Max Size the oldest go (counted on Dropped Items), under Flush Size, with Flush Interval above 0 and no timer running: a timer is armed to flush after Flush Interval → Overflowed, Done; Flushed stays silent

Data joins, past Max Size the oldest go (counted on Dropped Items), under Flush Size, with no timer to arm (Flush Interval 0, or one already running): it waits → Overflowed, Done; Flushed stays silent
Data joins and the buffer reaches Flush Size: it becomes Flushed Data, a fresh one starts, Flush Count grows, a running timer stops → Flushed, Done; Overflowed stays silent
Data joins, under Flush Size, with Flush Interval above 0 and no timer running: a timer is armed to flush after Flush Interval → Done; Overflowed, Flushed stay silent
Data joins, under Flush Size, with no timer to arm (Flush Interval 0, or one already running): it waits → Done; Overflowed, Flushed stay silent
flush: nothing buffered: nothing to hand over, and Flush Count stays → Unchanged; Flushed stays silent
anything buffered: it becomes Flushed Data, a fresh buffer starts, Flush Count grows, a running timer stops → Flushed, Done
clear: anything buffered, flushed or counted: the buffer, Flushed Data and both counts are emptied — not Error, not the Data retained — and a running timer stops → Cleared, Done
nothing held: the same empty values are sent again → Cleared, Unchanged

inputs.name: add
inputs.description: Appends the current Chunk, which is retained between pulses, so a second Add with no new chunk appends it again

inputs.name: chunk
inputs.description: The next fragment of text to append; wire a stream Text output, not its Data output, which is JSON-parsed and is usually an object

inputs.name: clear
inputs.description: Empties the buffer, the messages and both dropped counts

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: Message boundary to split complete messages off; leave empty to accumulate everything, which is what a token stream wants

inputs.name: maxLength
inputs.description: Cap on the pending buffer in characters; overflow drops the oldest and is counted on Dropped Characters

inputs.name: maxMessages
inputs.description: Cap on retained complete messages, oldest dropped first; 0 keeps them all, which grows forever

outputs.name: accumulated
outputs.description: Everything appended since the last Clear that has not yet been split off as a complete message

outputs.name: byteCount
outputs.description: Length of Accumulated in UTF-8 bytes, which differs from Character Count for anything outside ASCII

outputs.name: changed
outputs.description: Fires whenever an Add appended something, which is the cue to redraw

outputs.name: characterCount
outputs.description: Length of Accumulated in characters

outputs.name: cleared
outputs.description: Fires once the buffer and the messages have been emptied

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires once an Add or Clear you triggered has changed the buffer

outputs.name: droppedCharacters
outputs.description: How many characters Max Length has discarded from the front since the last Clear

outputs.name: droppedMessages
outputs.description: How many complete messages Max Messages has discarded since the last Clear

outputs.name: error
outputs.description: Why the last chunk was refused; blank once a chunk of text arrives

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when a chunk was not text and nothing was appended, which usually means the wrong stream output is wired

outputs.name: lastMessage
outputs.description: The most recent complete message, which is what a chat surface usually wants

outputs.name: messageCount
outputs.description: How many complete messages are being retained, which is not how many have arrived

outputs.name: messageReceived
outputs.description: Fires once per Add that completed at least one message, not once per message

outputs.name: messages
outputs.description: Complete messages split off the delimiter, oldest first, capped at Max Messages

outputs.name: overflowed
outputs.description: Fires when Max Length or Max Messages has just discarded something

outputs.name: unchanged
outputs.description: Fires when an Add had no text to append — an empty chunk, or one already refused — or a Clear found nothing to discard

chunk: text (a number, boolean or bigint as its text; nothing as empty) while an Error stands: kept for the next Add, and the Error is cleared → Failure stays silent
text (a number, boolean or bigint as its text; nothing as empty): kept for the next Add, and retained after it → Failure stays silent
an object, array or Date again, the same refusal already on Error: the chunk is emptied and nothing more is said → Failure stays silent
an object, array or Date: refused before any Add — the chunk is emptied and Error names what arrived → Failure
delimiter: always: read at the next Add — where complete messages are split off (nothing, or empty: never split)
maxLength: always: read at the next Add — the cap the oldest characters are dropped past (not above 0: no cap); a buffer already over it is trimmed by the next Add
maxMessages: always: read at the next Add that completes a message — the cap the oldest messages are dropped past (not at least 0: 0, keep all)
add: an empty Chunk (a keep-alive, or one that was refused): nothing is appended → Unchanged; Overflowed, Changed, Message Received stay silent

the chunk is appended, past Max Length the oldest characters go (counted on Dropped Characters), and no Delimiter completes a message: Accumulated grows → Overflowed, Changed, Done; Message Received stays silent
the chunk is appended and no Delimiter completes a message: Accumulated grows → Changed, Done; Overflowed, Message Received stay silent

the chunk is appended, past Max Length the oldest characters go (counted on Dropped Characters), a Delimiter completes a message, and past Max Messages the oldest messages go (counted on Dropped Messages): Overflowed twice, the last complete one is Last Message, the rest stays in Accumulated → Overflowed, Overflowed, Message Received, Changed, Done

the chunk is appended, a Delimiter completes a message, and past Max Messages the oldest messages go (counted on Dropped Messages): the last complete one is Last Message, the rest stays in Accumulated → Overflowed, Message Received, Changed, Done

the chunk is appended, past Max Length the oldest characters go (counted on Dropped Characters), and a Delimiter completes a message: it joins Messages, the last complete one is Last Message, the rest stays in Accumulated → Overflowed, Message Received, Changed, Done

the chunk is appended and a Delimiter completes a message: it joins Messages, the last complete one is Last Message, the rest stays in Accumulated — Message Received once however many completed → Message Received, Changed, Done; Overflowed stays silent
clear: anything accumulated, kept, dropped or refused: the buffer, Messages, Last Message, both dropped counts and the Error are emptied — not the Chunk retained → Cleared, Done
nothing held: the same empty values are sent again → Cleared, Unchanged

inputs.name: columns
inputs.description: Which properties to write, in order, comma separated. Leave it empty and every property found on the records is written, in the order they were first seen

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: The character between cells. Any cell containing it is quoted automatically

inputs.name: includeHeader
inputs.description: Write the column names as the first row

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: The array to write. Records become rows; an array of arrays is written cell for cell

outputs.name: changed
outputs.description: Fires once CSV holds the freshly written text

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: How many data rows were written, not counting the header row

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The array as CSV text. Cells containing the delimiter, a quote or a newline are quoted and their quotes doubled, so this round-trips back through Parse CSV unchanged

items: always: written at the end of the frame (once, however many inputs moved) — CSV, Count and Changed; nothing (undefined or null) is not written; rows that are all arrays go cell for cell with no header, anything else as records
columns: always: the Items are written again at the end of the frame, once any have arrived — these properties in this order (comma-separated, blanks dropped), or every property first seen when empty
delimiter: always: the Items are written again at the end of the frame, once any have arrived, with this between cells (cleared reads as a comma)
includeHeader: always: the Items are written again at the end of the frame, once any have arrived, with the column names as the first row or not — rows of cells never get one

inputs.name: generate
inputs.description: Generates a fresh UUID, replacing the one on Id

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires once a new UUID is available on Id

outputs.name: error
outputs.description: Why no UUID could be generated

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when there is no cryptographic random source here, leaving Id as it was

outputs.name: uuid
outputs.description: A random version-4 UUID, generated once when the node is created and again on every New. Use this rather than Unique Id wherever the id has to be globally unique or unguessable

generate: always: a fresh UUID goes on Id, and Error is cleared → Done

ssr.note: A WebSocket cannot be meaningfully opened during a server render and would leak a socket per request; the node connects in the browser after hydration.

inputs.name: autoConnect
inputs.description: Connect as soon as a URL is available, without waiting for a Connect signal

inputs.name: autoReconnect
inputs.description: Retries after an unsolicited close with a growing backoff; turning it off reports the close as an error

inputs.name: connect
inputs.description: Opens the socket, replacing one already open without reporting a close

inputs.name: disconnect
inputs.description: Closes the socket and cancels any pending reconnect

inputs.name: heartbeatInterval
inputs.description: Milliseconds between heartbeats while the socket is open; 0 disables it, and only enable it if your server expects the message

inputs.name: heartbeatMessage
inputs.description: Application text sent as the heartbeat; it is not a protocol ping frame

inputs.name: heartbeatReply
inputs.description: Exact text the server answers a heartbeat with; it is measured as Latency, hidden from On Message, and its absence is treated as a dead connection

inputs.name: jitter
inputs.description: Spreads reconnect attempts randomly across the second half of each backoff window, so a fleet does not return in lockstep

inputs.name: maxQueueSize
inputs.description: Messages the queue holds before further Sends are refused and counted as dropped; 0 or less is unlimited and can grow during a long outage

inputs.name: maxReconnectDelay
inputs.description: Ceiling on the backoff in milliseconds, however many attempts there have been

inputs.name: maxRetries
inputs.description: Reconnect attempts allowed per outage; 0 disables retrying and a negative value means unlimited

inputs.name: message
inputs.description: Value to send; objects are JSON-serialised, and ArrayBuffers and typed arrays go as binary frames

inputs.name: messageType
inputs.description: Auto sends binary values as binary and everything else as text; Binary encodes text and objects as UTF-8 first

inputs.name: protocols
inputs.description: Comma-separated WebSocket subprotocols to offer during the handshake

inputs.name: reconnectDelay
inputs.description: First backoff delay in milliseconds; each further attempt doubles it up to Max Reconnect Delay

inputs.name: send
inputs.description: Hands the current Message to the socket, or applies the When Disconnected policy

inputs.name: url
inputs.description: Endpoint to connect to, which must start with ws:// or wss://; changing it reconnects to the new one

inputs.name: whenDisconnected
inputs.description: What a Send does while the socket is not open: hold it in order, discard and count it, or also report an error

outputs.name: closeCode
outputs.description: WebSocket close code from the last close, or 1006 when the socket died without one

outputs.name: closeReason
outputs.description: Reason the server gave for closing, which is often blank

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: connected
outputs.description: True only while the socket is open and messages can be sent without queueing

outputs.name: connectionState
outputs.description: Where the connection is: idle, connecting, open, reconnecting, closed or error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires when the action finished: a Connect whose socket opened, a Send accepted for delivery (sent, or queued for the next open), or a Disconnect that closed something

outputs.name: droppedCount
outputs.description: Messages that will never be sent, whether discarded by policy, by a full queue, or by the node being removed

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when the action could not be performed — no URL, a URL that is not ws:// or wss://, a connection that gave up, or a refused Send. Last Error carries the reason

outputs.name: lastError
outputs.description: What went wrong most recently, including why a reconnect was scheduled or abandoned

outputs.name: latency
outputs.description: Round trip of the last heartbeat in milliseconds; 0 until one has been measured

outputs.name: onClose
outputs.description: Fires whenever the socket goes down, whether or not a reconnect is going to follow

outputs.name: onError
outputs.description: Fires when something went wrong: a failed connect, a refused send, a dead heartbeat, or a give-up

outputs.name: onMessage
outputs.description: Fires once per message, after Received already holds it; heartbeat replies are not messages

outputs.name: onMessageSent
outputs.description: Fires when a message has been handed to the socket, including a queued one flushed on reopen; not for heartbeats

outputs.name: onOpen
outputs.description: Fires every time the socket opens, including after a reconnect

outputs.name: onReconnect
outputs.description: Fires on every open after the first; a WebSocket cannot resume, so this is the cue to re-fetch rather than assume continuity

outputs.name: queueSize
outputs.description: Messages held because the socket was not open when Send ran

outputs.name: received
outputs.description: The last message, parsed as JSON when it is JSON and handed over as text when it is not

outputs.name: receivedIsBinary
outputs.description: True when the last message was a binary frame, in which case Received holds the buffer

outputs.name: receivedRaw
outputs.description: The last text message exactly as it arrived; blank for a binary frame

outputs.name: retryCount
outputs.description: Attempts made during the current outage; back to zero once the socket opens

outputs.name: unchanged
outputs.description: Fires when there was nothing to do: a Disconnect with nothing open, a Send discarded by the Drop policy, or a Connect a later Connect or Disconnect superseded before it opened

url: no connection yet: stored as text (nothing as blank); at the end of the frame one connects to it when Auto Connect is on and it is not blank — Connection State connecting, the Status outputs sent (a URL not starting with ws:// or wss:// fails at once instead: Connection State error, Last Error, On Error); with Auto Connect off it waits for a Connect
the URL the connection was made with (its Protocols too): stored; nothing else, now or at the end of the frame — a closed or failed connection is not retried by setting its URL again

a URL other than the connection's: stored; at the end of the frame that connection is dropped silently (its socket closed, its countdown and heartbeat stopped, no On Close; a Connect still waiting, or made before then against the old URL: Unchanged), the Status outputs sent, and a fresh one (Retry Count 0, Queue Size 0, Dropped 0) connects to this URL when it is not blank and Auto Connect is on or the old one was connecting, open or reconnecting — Connection State connecting (not starting with ws:// or wss://: error, Last Error, On Error); otherwise idle
autoConnect: on or off, with a connection (open, closed or failed alike): held for the next URL or Protocols change, after which the new one connects when this is on; nothing now or at the end of the frame — off closes nothing, on reopens nothing

on, with no connection yet: at the end of the frame one connects when the URL is not blank — Connection State connecting, the Status outputs sent (a URL not starting with ws:// or wss://: error, Last Error, On Error); a blank URL: idle until one arrives
off, with no connection yet: nothing — it waits for a Connect
protocols: no connection yet: split on commas and trimmed (blank or not text: none), offered at the handshake when a connection is made — at the end of the frame when Auto Connect is on and there is a URL, else at the next Connect
the list the connection was made with (its URL too): stored; nothing else, now or at the end of the frame

a list other than the connection's: stored; at the end of the frame that connection is dropped silently (no On Close; a Connect still waiting: Unchanged), the Status outputs sent, and a fresh one offering these connects when the URL is not blank and Auto Connect is on or the old one was connecting, open or reconnecting — Connection State connecting; otherwise idle
autoReconnect: on or off: onto the connection at once, read at its next unsolicited close — on, the drop is retried after the backoff wait (Connection State reconnecting, Last Error says when, On Close); off, it is final: a goodbye (1000 or 1001) is Connection State closed and On Close, anything else error, Last Error, On Error and On Close; a reconnect already counting down still fires either way
reconnectDelay: always: onto the connection at once, read when the next backoff is drawn — the first retry of an outage waits this many milliseconds, each later one twice the last, capped at Max Reconnect Delay (ms); 0, below, or not a number: 1000; a wait already counting down keeps its length
maxReconnectDelay: always: onto the connection at once, read when the next backoff is drawn — the ceiling on the wait in milliseconds, however many retries; 0, below, or not a number: 30000
maxRetries: always: onto the connection at once, read at its next unsolicited close — Retry Count (the retries so far in this outage) below it: one more; at it: gives up — Connection State error, Last Error `… gave up after n reconnect attempts`, On Error, On Close (a waiting Connect: Failure); 0, or not a number: no retry; below 0: unlimited; a close code retrying cannot help (1002, 1003, 1007 to 1010, 1015) gives up whatever this is
jitter: on or off: onto the connection at once, read when the next backoff is drawn — on, the wait is scaled by a random draw into its second half (from half of it to all of it); off, the whole wait exactly
heartbeatInterval: a different interval while the socket is open: the heartbeat restarts now — a reply still awaited is forgotten, and the Heartbeat Message goes this many milliseconds from now, then every interval; 0, below, or not a number: the heartbeat stops

the same interval, or no open socket: read when the socket next opens — above 0, the Heartbeat Message is sent every this many milliseconds (not On Message Sent) and the Heartbeat Reply swallowed; 0, below, or not a number: no heartbeat, and a Heartbeat Reply arriving is an ordinary message
heartbeatMessage: always: onto the connection at once (not text: blank), read at the next beat — the text sent as the heartbeat, not On Message Sent; blank: no beat is sent and no reply awaited, so no connection is declared dead
heartbeatReply: always: onto the connection at once (not text: blank), read at the next beat and the next message — while a heartbeat runs, a message equal to it is swallowed instead of On Message and, when a beat was awaiting it, measured as Latency (ms) (the Status outputs sent); a beat still unanswered when the next is due is a dead connection: Last Error, On Error, then handled as a 1006 close; blank: nothing is awaited
message: always: held for the next Send (nothing or null fails it)
messageType: always: onto the connection at once (nothing as Auto), read at the next send — Binary encodes text, and an object's JSON, as UTF-8 bytes; Auto and Text send them as text; a buffer or typed array goes as bytes whatever this says
whenDisconnected: always: onto the connection at once (nothing as Queue), read by the next Send while the socket is not open — Queue holds it in order (Done; sent at the next open), Drop discards it and counts it in Dropped (Unchanged), Report Error counts it and fails (Last Error, On Error, Failure websocket/not-connected); messages already queued stay queued
maxQueueSize: always: onto the connection at once, read by the next Send that would queue — above 0, a queue already this long refuses it: Dropped, Last Error, On Error, Failure websocket/queue-full; 0, below, or not a number: no limit; a queue already longer than a new limit keeps what it holds
connect: a blank URL: any socket held is closed quietly and the countdown and heartbeat stopped (a Connect still waiting: Unchanged), then it fails at once — Connection State error, Last Error `URL is required to connect`, Retry Count 0, the Status outputs sent, On Error; Failure (websocket/connect-failed)

a URL not starting with ws:// or wss://: any socket held is closed quietly (a Connect still waiting: Unchanged), then it fails at once — Connection State error, Last Error `URL must start with ws:// or wss://`, Retry Count 0, the Status outputs sent, On Error; Failure (websocket/connect-failed)

a URL the browser refuses to open: any socket held is closed quietly (a Connect still waiting: Unchanged), Connection State connecting, then error at once — Last Error `Could not open WebSocket: …`, Retry Count 0, the Status outputs sent, On Error; Failure (websocket/connect-failed)

a URL starting with ws:// or wss:// (the connection's own: one changed this frame is taken at the frame's end, which then supersedes this): any socket held is closed quietly, the countdown and heartbeat stopped (a Connect still waiting: Unchanged), Retry Count 0, Close Code 0, Connection State connecting (Connected false), the Status outputs sent, and a socket is made with the URL trimmed and the Protocols; settled later — Done when it opens (On Open, however many retried drops lie between), Failure (websocket/connect-failed) when the connection fails or gives up, Unchanged when a later Connect, a Disconnect or a URL change supersedes it
disconnect: no connection was ever made: nothing is sent (a Connect still waiting: Unchanged); Unchanged

a socket held, or a connection connecting, open or reconnecting: the socket is closed (1000 `Client disconnect`), the countdown and heartbeat stopped, nothing more arrives — Connection State closed, Connected false, Retry Count 0, Close Code 1000, Close Reason `Client disconnect`, the Status outputs sent, On Close (a Connect still waiting: Unchanged); Done

a connection idle, closed or failed, holding no socket: Connection State closed, Retry Count 0, Close Code 1000, Close Reason `Client disconnect` (Last Error kept), the Status outputs sent, no On Close; Unchanged
send: Message empty (nothing or null), whatever the socket is doing: Last Error `Nothing to send: the Message input is empty`, the Status outputs sent, On Error; Failure (websocket/nothing-to-send)

the socket not open (idle, connecting, reconnecting, closed or failed), When Disconnected Report Error: Dropped counts it, Last Error `Cannot send: the connection is not open`, the Status outputs sent, On Error; Failure (websocket/not-connected)

the socket not open, When Disconnected Queue, Max Queue Size above 0 and Queue Size at it: Dropped counts it, Last Error `Send queue is full`, the Status outputs sent, On Error; Failure (websocket/queue-full)
the socket not open, When Disconnected Drop: discarded — Dropped counts it, the Status outputs sent, no On Error; Unchanged

the socket not open (an idle connection is made if there is none), When Disconnected Queue, with room: held at the back of the queue — Queue Size, the Status outputs sent; sent in order when the socket next opens, On Message Sent for each then; Done

the socket open: handed to it now — text as itself, an object as JSON, anything else as text, a buffer or typed array as bytes, and with Message Type Binary the text as UTF-8 bytes — On Message Sent; the Status outputs stay silent; Done

ssr.note: The scheduler clock is frozen during server render; the value stays at its start and Finished never fires there.

targetValue: the first number it is handed: Current Value goes there at once, with no move
the target it already has: nothing
a new target: a move under way is dropped without At Target Value, and a new one starts from where the value is, at the frame's end and Delay later
jumpValue: always: kept for the next Jump To; nothing moves
jumpTo: Jump Value is not a number: nothing
no number yet: Current Value goes to Jump Value, which becomes the target too
otherwise: any move stops, Current Value goes to Jump Value, and at the frame's end it moves back to Target Value if they differ
duration: always: kept; read at every frame of a move, the move under way included
delay: always: kept as a number (what is not one is 0); read when the next move starts

dynamicPorts.description: Declares conditional/expandable port groups whose visibility depends on parameter values (see declaredPortGroups).

declaredPortGroups.condition: useLabel = true OR useLabel NOT SET
borderStyle = solid OR borderStyle = dashed OR borderStyle = dotted
borderLeftStyle = solid OR borderLeftStyle = dashed OR borderLeftStyle = dotted OR borderStyle = solid OR borderStyle = dashed OR borderStyle = dotted
borderTopStyle = solid OR borderTopStyle = dashed OR borderTopStyle = dotted OR borderStyle = solid OR borderStyle = dashed OR borderStyle = dotted
borderRightStyle = solid OR borderRightStyle = dashed OR borderRightStyle = dotted OR borderStyle = solid OR borderStyle = dashed OR borderStyle = dotted
borderBottomStyle = solid OR borderBottomStyle = dashed OR borderBottomStyle = dotted OR borderStyle = solid OR borderStyle = dashed OR borderStyle = dotted

accept.rule: a data attribute name: "data-", then a lowercase letter or digit, then lowercase letters, digits, ".", "_" or "-"

variables.name: one of the names listed in the `dataAttributes` parameter; a data attribute name: "data-", then a lowercase letter or digit, then lowercase letters, digits, ".", "_" or "-"

parameterEncoding.notes: Every port is listed in `inputs`/`outputs` above except the ones named by a list parameter (the patterns here): `dynamicPorts.declaredPortGroups` says which parameter values reveal which listed port, and holds the `namedports/derived` rule that turns each listed name into a port.

enabled: the value it already holds: nothing
a change: Enabled follows; disabled, it takes no click, no mouse press and no keyboard, but still hovers and still feels a finger
mounted: always: the element is put on the page (Did Mount), or taken off it (Will Unmount), at the next paint
focus: not on the page: nothing to focus, the Focus is not kept, and the editor is told → Unchanged; Focused stays silent
it holds the keyboard already, or is disabled or hidden: nothing changes → Done; Focused stays silent
otherwise the keyboard is put on it, and the Focused state goes true → Focused, Done
blur: it does not hold the keyboard (or is disabled, and gives it up to nobody): nothing changes → Done; Blurred stays silent
it holds the keyboard: it is taken off it, and the Focused state goes false → Blurred, Done
scrollIntoView: always: the page, or the scrolling Group holding it, scrolls until the button can be seen
visible: always: shown or hidden at the next paint, its space kept; hidden, a Focus does not reach it

parameterEncoding.notes: Every port is listed in `inputs`/`outputs` above except the ones named by a list parameter (the patterns here): `dynamicPorts.declaredPortGroups` says which parameter values reveal which listed port, and holds the `namedports/derived` rule that turns each listed name into a port.

enabled: the value it already holds: nothing
a change: Enabled follows; disabled, the box takes no click and no focus
checked: the value it already holds: nothing
a change: the box shows it, and Checked follows — Changed does not fire (only a person's click fires it)
check: unchecked: it is checked, and Checked goes true — never Changed → Done
uncheck: checked: it is unchecked, and Checked goes false — never Changed → Done
mounted: always: the box is put on the page (Did Mount), or taken off it (Will Unmount), at the next paint
useLabel: always: a label is drawn beside the box, or not; the box and its keyboard stay
focus: not on the page: nothing to focus, the Focus is not kept, and the editor is told → Unchanged; Focused stays silent
it holds the keyboard already, or is disabled or hidden: nothing changes → Done; Focused stays silent
otherwise the keyboard is put on it, and the Focused state goes true → Focused, Done
blur: it does not hold the keyboard (or is disabled, and gives it up to nobody): nothing changes → Done; Blurred stays silent
it holds the keyboard: it is taken off it, and the Focused state goes false → Blurred, Done
scrollIntoView: always: the page, or the scrolling Group holding it, scrolls until the box can be seen
visible: always: shown or hidden at the next paint, its space kept; hidden, a Focus does not reach it

dynamicPorts.description: The port list above is complete — this node mints no ports. It republishes its own `value` input per instance as an `enum` built from this node's `items`: one choice per option, labelled with the option's `Label` and carrying its `Value`, plus the currently stored value when that matches no option. It is declared `string` statically because nothing outside a connected editor can know the instance's options.

parameterEncoding.notes: This node mints no port names. Its `value` input is declared `string` above and is republished per instance as an `enum` whose choices are this node's own `items` — labels from each option's `Label`, values from its `Value` — so the port list above is complete and only the `type` field moves. A value that matches no option is offered back as a choice of its own rather than being dropped.

enabled: the value it already holds: nothing
a change: Enabled follows; disabled, the list takes no pick, no click and no focus
items: nothing handed (undefined): the list it has stays
otherwise: the list is kept as handed and drawn at the next paint; the value stays, so a list handed again keeps the pick
value: null: ignored
the value it already holds, as text: nothing
a change: kept as text, Value follows, and the list selects it at the next paint if it names an option — Changed does not fire (only a person's pick fires it)
mounted: always: the list is put on the page (Did Mount), or taken off it (Will Unmount), at the next paint
useLabel: always: a label is drawn beside the list, or not; the list, its keyboard and its pick stay
focus: not on the page: nothing to focus, the Focus is not kept, and the editor is told → Unchanged; Focused stays silent
it holds the keyboard already, or is disabled or hidden: nothing changes → Done; Focused stays silent
otherwise the keyboard is put on it, and the Focused state goes true → Focused, Done
blur: it does not hold the keyboard (or is disabled, and gives it up to nobody): nothing changes → Done; Blurred stays silent
it holds the keyboard: it is taken off it, and the Focused state goes false → Blurred, Done
scrollIntoView: always: the page, or the scrolling Group holding it, scrolls until the list can be seen
visible: always: shown or hidden at the next paint, its space kept; hidden, a Focus does not reach it

parameterEncoding.notes: Every port is listed in `inputs`/`outputs` above except the ones named by a list parameter (the patterns here): `dynamicPorts.declaredPortGroups` says which parameter values reveal which listed port, and holds the `namedports/derived` rule that turns each listed name into a port.

enabled: the value it already holds: nothing
a change: Enabled follows; disabled, the button takes no click and no focus
value: always: what this button contributes when selected; at the next paint it shows selected when its group's Value is this and not otherwise — Checked follows, Changed does not fire
mounted: always: the button is put on the page (Did Mount, showing its group's choice — Checked follows without Changed), or taken off it (Will Unmount, with the keyboard and the states it held), at the next paint
useLabel: always: a label is drawn beside the button, or not; the button and its keyboard stay
focus: not on the page: nothing to focus, the Focus is not kept, and the editor is told → Unchanged; Focused stays silent
it holds the keyboard already, or is disabled or hidden: nothing changes → Done; Focused stays silent
otherwise the keyboard is put on it, and the Focused state goes true → Focused, Done
blur: it does not hold the keyboard (or is disabled, and gives it up to nobody): nothing changes → Done; Blurred stays silent
it holds the keyboard: it is taken off it, and the Focused state goes false → Blurred, Done
scrollIntoView: always: the page, or the scrolling Group holding it, scrolls until the button can be seen
visible: always: shown or hidden at the next paint, its space kept; hidden, it takes no click and a Focus does not reach it

enabled: the value it already holds: nothing
a change: Enabled follows; disabled, the handle takes no slide and no focus
value: empty: no word, and the handle stays where it is
not a number: no word, the editor is told, and the handle stays where it is

a number: at the next paint the handle goes there, clamped to Min and Max and rounded to the Step; Value and Value Percent follow when they move — Changed does not fire (only a person's slide fires it)
min: always: at the next paint the handle is held at or above it (an empty Min is 0) and on the Step; Value and Value Percent follow when they move — never Changed
max: always: at the next paint the handle is held at or below it (an empty Max is 100; below Min, the handle holds Min) and on the Step; Value and Value Percent follow when they move — never Changed
step: always: at the next paint the handle is rounded to it (one that is not above 0 is 1); Value and Value Percent follow when they move — never Changed
mounted: always: the slider is put on the page (Did Mount), or taken off it (Will Unmount), at the next paint; put back, the handle is where it was left
focus: not on the page: nothing to focus, the Focus is not kept, and the editor is told → Unchanged; Focused stays silent
it holds the keyboard already, or is disabled or hidden: nothing changes → Done; Focused stays silent
otherwise the keyboard is put on it, and the Focused state goes true → Focused, Done
blur: it does not hold the keyboard (or is disabled, and gives it up to nobody): nothing changes → Done; Blurred stays silent
it holds the keyboard: it is taken off it, and the Focused state goes false → Blurred, Done
scrollIntoView: always: the page, or the scrolling Group holding it, scrolls until the slider can be seen
visible: always: shown or hidden at the next paint, its space kept; hidden, a Focus does not reach it

dynamicPorts.description: The port list above is complete — this node mints no ports. It republishes its own two value ports (`startValue`, `onTextChanged`) per instance with a narrowed type: `number` when the `type` parameter is `number`, `string` for every other Type. They are declared `*` statically because nothing outside a connected editor can narrow them.

declaredPortGroups.condition: borderStyle = solid OR borderStyle = dashed OR borderStyle = dotted
borderLeftStyle = solid OR borderLeftStyle = dashed OR borderLeftStyle = dotted OR borderStyle = solid OR borderStyle = dashed OR borderStyle = dotted
borderTopStyle = solid OR borderTopStyle = dashed OR borderTopStyle = dotted OR borderStyle = solid OR borderStyle = dashed OR borderStyle = dotted
borderRightStyle = solid OR borderRightStyle = dashed OR borderRightStyle = dotted OR borderStyle = solid OR borderStyle = dashed OR borderStyle = dotted
borderBottomStyle = solid OR borderBottomStyle = dashed OR borderBottomStyle = dotted OR borderStyle = solid OR borderStyle = dashed OR borderStyle = dotted

accept.rule: a data attribute name: "data-", then a lowercase letter or digit, then lowercase letters, digits, ".", "_" or "-"

variables.name: one of the names listed in the `dataAttributes` parameter; a data attribute name: "data-", then a lowercase letter or digit, then lowercase letters, digits, ".", "_" or "-"

parameterEncoding.notes: This node mints no port names. Its two value ports are declared `'*'` above and are republished per instance with a narrowed type — `number` when the `type` parameter is `number`, `string` otherwise — so the port list above is complete and only the `type` field moves.

enabled: the value it already holds: nothing
a change: Enabled follows; disabled, the field takes no typing, no key and no focus
type: always: read at the next paint and the next write — what the field accepts, and whether Value hands on a number or text
startValue: the value it already holds (null as empty): nothing
a new value, with Run On Value Change unticked: held for the next Set
a new value, with Run On Value Change ticked: written now — on the page the field takes it (Value, Value Changed) unless it holds the keyboard; off the page Value alone, when it differs
runOnChange-startValue: always: whether a new Value is written at once, or waits for Set
set: always: at the end of the frame (or a pointer act's drain before it) the Value as it stands is written, as a ticked Value writes it — Done if it wrote, else Unchanged
textToInsert: always: read by the next Insert Text, as text (nothing as empty)
insert: always: at the end of the frame Text To Insert goes in at the caret (at the end, off the page), within Max length — Value, Value Changed on the page, and Done; Unchanged when nothing fits
backspace: always, at once: the character before the caret goes (the last one, off the page) — Value, Value Changed on the page, and Done; Unchanged when there is none
clear: always, at once: the field and Value are emptied (Value Changed on the page, focused or not) — Done; Unchanged when they were empty already
maxLength: always: read at the next keystroke and Insert Text — above 0, no more characters than this
mounted: always: the field is put on the page (Did Mount), or taken off it (Will Unmount), at the next paint
useLabel: always: a label is drawn above the field, or not; the field and its keyboard stay
focus: not on the page: nothing to focus, the Focus is not kept, and the editor is told → Unchanged; Focused stays silent
it holds the keyboard already, or is disabled or hidden: nothing changes → Done; Focused stays silent
otherwise the keyboard is put on it, and the Focused state goes true → Focused, Done
blur: it does not hold the keyboard (or is disabled, and gives it up to nobody): nothing changes → Done; Blurred stays silent
it holds the keyboard: it is taken off it, and the Focused state goes false → Blurred, Done
scrollIntoView: always: the page, or the scrolling Group holding it, scrolls until the field can be seen
blockTouch: always: on, a pointer act that lands here goes no further — the nodes it sits inside do not hear it
visible: always: shown or hidden at the next paint, its space kept; hidden, a Focus does not reach it
opacity: always: how see-through it is; at exactly 0 it takes no pointer, and an act goes to what is behind it

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires once the link has been handed to the browser. It does not promise a tab appeared — nothing readable in the page does, once Open In New Tab is on. With it off the page is replaced, so nothing downstream of this may still exist

outputs.description: Why the link could not be opened, set just before Failure fires

outputs.description: Fires when no Link was set, or when the link was opened outside a user action — the case a browser refuses a new tab for. A tab blocked for any other reason still reports Done

link: always: kept; read by the next Do
openInNewTab: always: kept; read by the next Do
do: no browser window (a server render): nothing opens → Unchanged
no Link: Error says so, and nothing opens → Failure
a new tab asked for outside a person's click or key: the browser blocks it, and Error says so → Failure
otherwise: Link opens, in a new tab unless Open In New Tab is off → Done

verify: always: one check at the end of the frame however many presses — verified: Valid true, Claims the payload, Error cleared, Done per press; refused: Valid false, the reason on Error, Claims untouched, Failure per press

inputs.name: limit
inputs.description: How many members to return in one call; Total still reports the whole membership, so a clipped page is always visible as one

inputs.name: read
inputs.description: Reads the members of the role

inputs.name: role
inputs.description: Name of the role to list the members of, matching the name a permission rule uses after "role:" — letters, digits, underscore and hyphen only

inputs.name: skip
inputs.description: How many members to step over before this page — Skip 100 with Limit 100 is the second page

inputs.name: treatUnchangedAs
inputs.description: What this node reports when the action was valid and there was nothing to do. Unchanged (the default) keeps it a third outcome of its own. Done suits a project whose chains should carry on either way; Failure suits one whose idiom is that a no-op is a bug. Completed fires whatever this is set to.

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires once Users and User Ids hold this page of the role membership

outputs.name: error
outputs.description: Why the last operation could not be performed

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when the members could not be read — a blank Role, an unusable name, or a role that does not exist

outputs.name: total
outputs.description: How many members the role has in total, before Limit — compare it with the length of Users to know whether there is another page

outputs.name: unchanged
outputs.description: Fires when the role exists and has no members at all — the "nobody has joined yet" branch

outputs.name: userIds
outputs.description: Object ids of the members in this page, in the same order as Users

outputs.name: users
outputs.description: The member records for this page, shaped exactly like the account record /users/me answers with, so a For Each over them reads the same property names the User node does

role: always: read at the end of the frame by a Do pressed in it — blank fails that Do
limit: always: read at the end of the frame by a Do pressed in it, handed to the store as is
skip: always: read at the end of the frame by a Do pressed in it, handed to the store as is
treatUnchangedAs: always: read when an Unchanged is reported

inputs.name: apiKeySecret
inputs.description: The NAME of a secret in the project's functions namespace — never the key itself. It is read server-side at the moment of the call, exactly as the Secret node reads one, used in one header and dropped. There is deliberately no port that could hold the value. With OpenAI-compatible and a Base URL on this computer, a secret that is not provisioned means no key is sent; anywhere else a missing secret fails with secret_missing

inputs.name: baseUrl
inputs.description: Where the request goes. Change it for a local model server, a proxy, a gateway, or a test double. For OpenAI-compatible, a URL ending in /v1 or /chat/completions is used as given

inputs.name: callInstructions
inputs.description: More instructions that change from call to call — who this learner is, what happened last time. Sent after Instructions and never cached, so changing them does not throw the cached Instructions away

inputs.name: effort
inputs.description: How hard the model works before answering — the first lever to reach for on both cost and quality. Low for tagging and classifying, high for anything that has to be right. OpenAI-compatible: only None is sent (as reasoning_effort none), and it is the setting a small thinking model on this computer needs — without it a Qwen 3 spends a short Max Tokens thinking and answers nothing; the other values are not sent, because a model that does not think refuses them. Anthropic: None is sent as Low, the lowest it takes

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: The one thing being asked, as a single user turn. Ignored when Messages is wired — a graph holding a conversation sends the whole conversation

inputs.name: instructions
inputs.description: The system prompt — who the model is being asked to be, and the rules of the task. Cached: the first call writes it to the provider's prompt cache and calls in the next 5 minutes read it at a tenth of the price. Keep it the same on every call; anything that changes per call (a name, today's date) belongs in Per-Call Instructions or Input, or nothing is ever read back. Instructions shorter than the model's minimum (512 tokens on Claude Opus 5, up to 4,096 on some older models) are not cached at all: the call works, and Usage shows 0 written. OpenAI-compatible: Instructions and Per-Call Instructions are sent as one system message, and any caching is the server's own

inputs.name: maxTokens
inputs.description: The ceiling on the answer. Hitting it is not an error: Done fires with Stop Reason set to max_tokens and a truncated Text, so the graph can decide what that means

inputs.name: messages
inputs.description: A whole conversation as [{ role, content }], for a graph that is holding one. When this is wired and non-empty it replaces Input entirely

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model id, sent verbatim. Free text on purpose: a model released after this backend was built needs no release of NodeGX to be usable

inputs.name: outputSchema
inputs.description: A JSON schema the answer must match. When set, the answer is constrained to it and arrives parsed on Json as well as raw on Text. Objects in the schema need additionalProperties false, and the provider refuses the request outright if they do not have it. An OpenAI-compatible server is sent it as response_format json_schema; a server that ignores it and answers in prose fails with bad_json, and an answer that parses is not re-checked against the schema here

inputs.name: provider
inputs.description: Which API shape the request is built in. OpenAI-compatible is what a model running on your own computer speaks (Ollama, llama.cpp's server, LM Studio): point Base URL at it, for example http://127.0.0.1:11434, and set Model to the name that server knows the model by. A key is optional only when Base URL is this computer (127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost)

inputs.name: send
inputs.description: Sends the request

inputs.name: timeoutMs
inputs.description: The whole call's budget, retries included. Keep it under the function's own timeout, or the function answers 504 before this node gets to report anything

outputs.name: attempts
outputs.description: How many HTTP requests this call actually took. More than one means the provider rate-limited or faulted and the node retried; it is the number to watch before raising a quota

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires once the model has answered and Text, Json, Usage and Stop Reason hold that answer

outputs.name: error
outputs.description: Why there is no answer, in a sentence. Names the secret or the status, never a key. When the provider answered with an error, its own words follow — here only, never on the execution record, because a server's error can quote the request

outputs.name: errorCode
outputs.description: A stable code for the failure, for a graph that branches rather than reads: not_implemented, secret_missing, refusal, bad_json, http_error, rate_limited, timeout, network, unavailable

outputs.name: failure
outputs.description: Fires when no answer was obtained — a missing secret, a refusal, a provider error that outlived its retries, or an answer that did not match the schema. Read Error Code to tell them apart rather than matching on Error, which is written for a person

outputs.name: json
outputs.description: The answer parsed, when Output Schema asked for one. Untouched when no schema was set — a graph that wants an object has to say what shape it is

outputs.name: status
outputs.description: The HTTP status of the last attempt, or 0 when the request never reached the provider — a missing secret, a provider this node does not know, a timeout

outputs.name: stopReason
outputs.description: Why the model stopped: end_turn when it finished, max_tokens when it ran out of room, tool_use when it wants a tool. A refusal never arrives here — it fires Failure

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The model's answer. When Output Schema is set this is the raw JSON of it

outputs.name: usage
outputs.description: What the call cost, as { inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheWriteTokens }. A write on every call and reads of 0 means Instructions differ between calls. The same numbers land on the run's execution record, where they are summed per run

provider: always: read when the call is made — blank is Anthropic
model: always: read when the request is built — blank is the default model
apiKeySecret: always: the name read from the secret store when the call is made
baseUrl: always: read when the call is made — blank is the Anthropic API
instructions: always: read when the request is built
callInstructions: always: read when the request is built
input: always: read when the request is built, unless Messages holds a conversation
messages: always: read when the request is built — a non-empty list replaces Input
outputSchema: always: read when the request is built and again when its answer lands
effort: always: read when the request is built — blank is high
maxTokens: always: a positive number, floored, read when the request is built — anything else is 16000
timeoutMs: always: a positive number, floored, read when the call starts and in its timeout sentence — anything else is 120000
send: always: one call at the end of the frame however many presses — Done with the answer published, or Failure with Error, Error Code and Status, per press

role: always: read at the end of the frame by a Do pressed in it — blank fails that Do
